description: Cluster discovery through the neutral name, as the Use cases page describes it: no provider; an available provider with an empty inventory; one healthy single-node K3s cluster with its resources, events and keys; the cluster's server stopped; the provider unreachable (a failed probe), then back.

inputs.agent: the dev VM's production-style system unit opute-bootstrap-mcp.service (Rust 0.3.0 release candidate binary, test identity e2e-devvm-agent, test token), with the Rust k3s provider 1.0.2 from the release (e2e-provider-k3s, port 4320)
inputs.k3s: K3s v1.31.8+k3s1, downloaded by the provider from the K3s GitHub release and checked against its checksums; images pulled by K3s from public registries

requirements.requirement: A K3s server provisioned through typed Host Agent operations
requirements.scenario: The single-node cluster the journey runs on

requirements.spec: published docs, host-agents c9f9e775 (v0.2.4) site/public/use-cases/ ("Discover Kubernetes clusters when configured")
requirements.requirement: An empty inventory and a failed inventory probe are different outcomes

pass.equals: Error: no active Kubernetes provider is installed

requirements.scenario: No provider, an available provider with no cluster, one healthy cluster, and an unreachable provider: the empty inventory is a successful result with no clusters, the failed probe an error result

requirements.spec: published docs, host-agents c9f9e775 (v0.2.4) site/public/use-cases/ ("Discover Kubernetes clusters when configured")
requirements.requirement: Discovery under the name tools/list resolves
requirements.scenario: The page names list_kubernetes_clusters, Go v0.2.4's published name and the deployed product's. Rust's tools/list resolves discovery to the neutral list_compute_clusters (D22); the Go name is a hidden alias until cutover, so the page must change with the cutover

requirements.spec: the agent's published tools/list (inputSchema, outputSchema, description) for the tool named
requirements.requirement: list_namespaces, list_pods, list_services, list_cluster_events on a discovered cluster
requirements.scenario: Resources and events of the discovered cluster are read through typed calls

requirements.spec: the agent's published tools/list (inputSchema, outputSchema, description) for the tool named
requirements.requirement: A probe of a stopped cluster fails closed
requirements.scenario: With its server stopped, reading the cluster's events fails closed with an error result

requirements.requirement: A stopped cluster never reads as an empty inventory
requirements.scenario: With its only server stopped, the registered cluster is listed with its instance status and no node data (D28)

requirements.requirement: Every capability has its three roles

pass.equals: Error: list_configmap_keys is not implemented by this Host Agent build
Error: list_secret_keys is not implemented by this Host Agent build

requirements.scenario: The e2e-3 goal lists config and secret keys: both tools are published but have no provider in Rust and no handler in Go v0.2.4, so they fail closed (Q18)
No discovery result, state row or journal line carries the cluster's join token

steps.guest: chown -R opute /home/opute/.config/opute-e2e && systemd-run --collect --unit=e2e-provider-k3s --uid=opute --gid=opute --setenv=HOME=/home/opute --setenv=OPUTE_PROVIDER_PORT=4320 --property=Restart=no /opt/opute-e2e/providers/opute-provider-k3s >/dev/null && for i in $(seq 60); do ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | grep -q . && break; sleep 0.5; done; ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | wc -l

python3 -c 'import sys, time, json; sys.path.insert(0, "/opt/opute-e2e/guest"); import mcpwire
for i in range(120):
    r = mcpwire.mcp(3014, sys.argv[1], "tools/list", request_id=i + 1)
    names = [t["name"] for t in ((r.get("body") or {}).get("result") or {}).get("tools") or []]
    if "opute.capability.kubernetes.provision" in names: break
    time.sleep(0.5)
print(json.dumps({"listed": "opute.capability.kubernetes.provision" in names, "tools": len(names), "polls": i + 1}))' '${TOKEN}'

python3 -c 'import sys, json; sys.path.insert(0, "/opt/opute-e2e/guest"); import mcpwire
r = mcpwire.mcp(3014, sys.argv[1], "tools/list", request_id=1)
names = {t["name"] for t in r["body"]["result"]["tools"]}
print(json.dumps({n: n in names for n in ("list_compute_clusters", "list_kubernetes_clusters")}))' '${TOKEN}'

systemd-run --collect --unit=e2e-provider-k3s --uid=opute --gid=opute --setenv=HOME=/home/opute --setenv=OPUTE_PROVIDER_PORT=4320 --property=Restart=no /opt/opute-e2e/providers/opute-provider-k3s >/dev/null && for i in $(seq 60); do ss -ltnH 'sport = :4320' | grep -q . && break; sleep 0.5; done; echo started

{ grep -a -r -o -F '${K3S_TOKEN}' /home/opute/.config/opute 2>/dev/null; for u in opute-bootstrap-mcp e2e-provider-k3s; do journalctl -u $u --no-pager -o cat; done | grep -o -F '${K3S_TOKEN}'; } | wc -l

cleanup.guest: systemctl stop e2e-provider-k3s 2>/dev/null; incus delete -f e2e-k1 2>/dev/null; incus storage volume list default -f csv | awk -F, '$1=="image"{print $2}' | xargs -r -I{} incus storage volume delete default image/{}; rm -rf /home/opute/.config/opute-e2e /opt/opute-e2e/providers; true
